evidence.quote: | Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Tier 2 now decides the blocking rule for borrow, hold and renew, using the existing Accounts.isBlocked/Policy.blockingBalance and a new Accounts.ensureNotBlocked guard. The change also removes the existing CLI rule ('if fines - paid >= 5.00m then ...'), so the rule is no longer decided in Tier 4. The Tier 3 views (standing, members) and the CLI renderers only use Accounts.isBlocked or the view's Blocked flag. They do not re-derive the rule.

evidence.quote:
let renew ports (copyId: string) : Result<Views.RenewView, LendingError> =
    commit ports (fun today library ->
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Tier 1/2 gets no new effect. The guards are pure functions of the Library value. The new standing query and the reworked renew both go through the Tier 3 query/commit helpers, which use the Store and Clock ports. The CLI used to call ports.Store.Load()/Save, ports.Clock() and Loans.renew directly. The change removes that and so fixes a pre-existing Tier 4 to Tier 2 re-entry instead of adding one.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}
ensure (not (isBlocked memberId library)) (MemberBlocked(memberId, owed memberId library, activity))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Policy.blockingBalance is the only definition of the threshold, and every use references it. The 5.00m literal and the fines-minus-payments calculation in the CLI were duplicates, and the change deletes them. The amount owed comes only from Accounts.owed. The refusal message refers to the policy value rather than restating it.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The threshold for each member type is defined in Tier 2 (Policy.blockingBalance) and applied in Tier 2 (Accounts.blockingBalanceOf/isBlocked/ensureNotBlocked). The Tier 3 code that changed only formats the limit carried in the error. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code decides anything about the threshold.

evidence.quote: | MemberBlocked of MemberId * owed: decimal * limit: decimal * BlockedActivity

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The changes are pure: a policy function, Tier 2 lookups over the Library value, and a Tier 1 error case that gains a data field. No effect, port or Tier 4 code is added or changed.

evidence.quote:
let blockingBalance memberType =
    match memberType with
    | Standard -> 5.00m
    | Student -> 2.00m
    | Staff -> 10.00m
blocked until it is below {money limit}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The amounts for each member type are defined once, in Policy.blockingBalance. The refusal text now uses the limit that Tier 2 computed and carries in MemberBlocked, instead of reading the policy again in Tier 3. The single definition therefore drives both the decision and the message. No literal is copied anywhere else in production code.
